questions.q: What problem does an exposure solve, according to this lesson?
options: It replaces the need for generic and singular tests
It automatically builds a Power BI dashboard from a dbt model
It converts a mart into an incremental model
It makes a downstream consumer's dependency on dbt models (like a Power BI dashboard) a real, version-controlled fact inside the project, instead of living only in someone's memory
questions.explain: Without an exposure, the connection between a model and its downstream consumer is invisible to dbt and to anyone reading the project.

questions.q: Which properties are required when declaring an exposure?
options: name, type, and owner
url and maturity only
Only a description is required; everything else is optional
depends_on and label only
questions.explain: name, type (dashboard, notebook, analysis, ml, or application), and owner are the required properties per dbt's real exposure spec.

questions.q: What can an exposure's `depends_on` list actually reference?
options: Only raw table names as plain strings
Only other exposures, never models or sources
Any real ref(), source(), or metric() call — the same functions used inside models
Nothing — depends_on is a deprecated, unused property
questions.explain: dbt Labs' real example shows depends_on referencing ref('fct_orders'), source('gsheets', 'goals'), and metric('count_orders') together.

questions.q: What does the `+` mean in `dbt run -s +exposure:weekly_jaffle_metrics`?
options: Force a full refresh of the entire warehouse
Run the exposure twice for redundancy
Run everything upstream of that exposure — the exact chain of models that feeds it
Skip all tests during the run
questions.explain: The + selects the exposure's full upstream dependency chain, letting you test exactly what feeds one dashboard without running the whole project.

questions.q: How does an exposure appear inside the generated dbt docs site, according to this lesson?
options: Exposures do not appear in the docs site at all
Only as a line item in a separate billing report
As a red warning icon indicating a broken model
In a dedicated Exposures section listing each one, and as its own node in the lineage graph marked with an orange EXP indicator
questions.explain: Real screenshots from dbt's own docs show both: a dedicated exposures list under the project name, and an orange EXP-tagged node in the DAG itself.
